'''Jalen Derale Wilson''' (born November 4, 2000)<ref>{{cite web |title=Jalen Wilson |url=https://basketball.usbasket.com/player/Jalen-Wilson/B12/University-of-Kansas/420988 |website=US Basket |access-date=March 10, 2022}}</ref> is an American [[college basketball]] player at the [[University of Kansas]]. He was named a consensus first-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] his junior year.<ref>{{cite news|last=DeCourcy|first=Mike|title=Sporting News 2022-23 college basketball All-America team|date=March 7, 2023|url=https://www.sportingnews.com/ca/ncaa-basketball/news/sporting-news-2022-23-college-basketball-all-america-team/ynhqsffrvax9novxmglr2fgo|work=[[Sporting News]]|access-date=March 7, 2023}}</ref>

==High school career==
Wilson attended [[John H. Guyer High School]] in [[Denton, Texas]]. As a junior, averaged 16.1 points, 6.2 rebounds, 3.3 assists per game. As a senior, he averaged 18.1 points, 7.5 rebounds and three assists per game, earning Class 6A All-State honors.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Galloway |first1=Matt |title=Bill Self: Newest KU basketball signee Jalen Wilson to bring ‘incredible toughness’ |url=https://www.cjonline.com/sports/20190612/bill-self-newest-ku-basketball-signee-jalen-wilson-to-bring-incredible-toughness |website=[[The Topeka Capital-Journal]] |access-date=January 12, 2021 |date=June 12, 2019}}</ref>

===Recruiting===
Wilson was a consensus four-star [[College recruiting|recruit]] and was considered the 46th-best player in the 2019 class by [[247Sports.com|247Sports]]. He originally committed to playing college basketball for [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]] but reopened his recruitment with the departure of head coach [[John Beilein]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hoyt |first1=Joseph |title=Denton Guyer's Jalen Wilson requests release from Michigan days after John Beilein heads to Cleveland Cavaliers |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/high-school-sports/2019/05/16/denton-guyer-s-jalen-wilson-requests-release-from-michigan-days-after-john-beilein-heads-to-cleveland-cavaliers/ |website=[[The Dallas Morning News]] |access-date=January 12, 2021 |date=May 16, 2019}}</ref> He later committed to [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] over an offer from [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]], among others.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gosset |first1=Brian |title=From one basketball power to another: Guyer 4-star SF Jalen Wilson is headed to Big 12 |url=https://www.star-telegram.com/sports/dfwvarsity/article231482188.html |website=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]] |access-date=January 12, 2021 |date=June 12, 2019}}</ref>

==College career==
On November 8, 2019, Wilson suffered a broken ankle against [[UNC Greensboro Spartans men's basketball|UNC Greensboro]] in his second career game. He missed the remainder of the season and was granted a medical [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] after undergoing surgery.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Blen |first1=Max |title='I’ve been waiting a long time': New look Jalen Wilson is ready to play again for KU |url=https://www.kansan.com/sports/i-ve-been-waiting-a-long-time-new-look-jalen-wilson-is-ready-to-play/article_42a49bc4-2cfe-11eb-b1cc-7360e76bf5f1.html |website=[[The University Daily Kansan]] |access-date=January 12, 2021 |date=November 23, 2020}}</ref> On December 8, 2020, Wilson recorded 23 points and 10 rebounds, making a go-ahead three-pointer with 42 seconds remaining, in a 73–72 win over eighth-ranked [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Skretta |first1=Dave |title=Wilson hits go-ahead 3 in closing seconds as Kansas defeats Creighton 73-72 |url=https://www.foxsports.com/kansas-city/story/jalen-wilson-go-ahead-3-pointer-kansas-jayhawks-win-creighton-bluejays-120820 |website=Fox Sports |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=January 12, 2021 |date=December 8, 2020}}</ref> As a freshman, Wilson averaged 11.8 points and 7.9 rebounds per game, earning [[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] All-Freshman Team honors. On April 9, 2021, he declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]] while maintaining his college eligibility.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jalen Wilson declares for 2021 NBA Draft, will retain eligibility |url=https://www.kansan.com/sports/jalen-wilson-declares-for-2021-nba-draft-will-retain-eligibility/article_2c7b9df0-9970-11eb-b82d-b3c440eae776.html |website=[[The University Daily Kansan]] |access-date=May 30, 2021 |date=April 9, 2021}}</ref> Wilson ultimately returned to Kansas. On November 2, he was suspended for three games due to an arrest on suspicion of DUI.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=Kansas' Jalen Wilson suspended 3 regular-season games following DUI arrest |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/32535533/kansas-jalen-wilson-suspended-3-regular-season-games-following-dui-arrest |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=November 3, 2021 |date=November 2, 2021}}</ref> Wilson was named to the Third Team All-Big 12 as a sophomore.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Swain |first1=Michael |title=Ochai Agbaji named Big 12 POY as five other Jayhawks earn conference honors |url=https://247sports.com/college/kansas/Article/Ochai-Agbaji-Big-12-Player-of-the-Year-KU-basketball-All-Big-12-teams-Christian-Braun-David-McCormack-Jalen-Wilson-183978357/ |access-date=March 10, 2022 |work=247 Sports |date=March 6, 2022}}</ref> He averaged 11.1 points and 7.4 rebounds per game, helping the Jayhawks win a national title. Following the season Wilson declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]] but ultimately withdrew from the draft.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Tait |first1=Matt |title=Kansas forward Jalen Wilson withdraws from NBA draft, will return to KU for 2022-23 season |url=https://www2.kusports.com/news/2022/jun/01/kansas-forward-jalen-wilson-withdraws-nba-draft-wi/ |website=[[Kansas Jayhawks]] |access-date=March 5, 2023 |date=June 1, 2022}}</ref> As a junior, Wilson was named [[Big 12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big 12 Player of the Year]].<ref name=Big12awards>{{cite press release|url= https://big12sports.com/news/2023/3/5/phillips-66-all-big-12-mens-basketball-awards-announced.aspx |title= Phillips 66 All-Big 12 Men’s Basketball Awards Announced|publisher=Big 12 Conference |date=March 5, 2023 |access-date=March 5, 2023}}</ref>
